text:
maria: FYI a private/VPC customer just hit a regression after a host driver+kernel update. They upgraded from NVIDIA 525.x on Ubuntu 22.04 (5.15) to 535.x + kernel 6.1 and started seeing NCCL hangs/timeouts and model inference failures.

maria: Relevant excerpt from their node logs: 
```
[2026-05-12T09:03:21Z] ncclOpCheck FAILED: unhandled operation -1 (timeout)
E NCCLCommInitRank failed: unhandled error 3
[2026-05-12T09:03:22Z] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[2026-05-12T09:03:23Z] device_mmap_fault: 0000:65:00.0: failed to mmap BAR0 - -22
```

aj: Oof. Do they have driver pinned in their private deployment config?

maria: They said they followed the Private install guide, which mentions "recommended" drivers but doesn't strictly pin. Customer claims our public support matrix lists CUDA 12 / driver 535 as compatible with the model runtimes.

kevin: Common failure mode: kernel ABI mismatch + dkms module not rebuilt -> NVML or driver ops fail. The BAR0 mmap -22 looks like pci resource mapping failed after kernel change.

tara-support: Customer is pushing back, says "Redwood told us CUDA12+ was fine" and they want us to either validate or provide rollback instructions. We need clarity on what we guarantee for on-prem matrices.

leo-sre: Can we reproduce? Do we have a 6.1 + 535 test node in our private test fleet?

deploy-bot: Deployment note: there was a scheduled kernel rollout to a small subset of private test hosts yesterday at 02:12 UTC (job id job-rt-4971).

maria: We don't have an exact repro yet. Customer offered access to a failing node if we want to inspect.

aj: First troubleshooting steps: 1) confirm kernel module versions (nvidia.ko, nvidia-drm.ko) 2) check dmesg for "API mismatch"/"procfs" messages 3) ensure nvidia-smi works and shows expected driver.

kevin: Also verify NCCL ABI compatibility between our runtime (libnccl shipped in container) and the driver. Mismatched libcuda vs driver can give weird timeout behavior.

maria: Quick commands the customer ran and posted: 
```
$ nvidia-smi
Tue May 12 09:03:20 2026
Driver Version: 535.86.10
CUDA Version: 12.2

$ lsmod | grep nvidia
nvidia_drm 45056 0
nvidia_modeset 200704 1 nvidia_drm
nvidia 13631424 2 nvidia_modeset,nvidia_uvm
```

tara-support: They also included a container log where ncclInit() returns errors.

maria: Customer says they rolled the host drivers themselves (not via Redwood tooling) and expect Redwood to support their configuration for Private.

leo-sre: Important policy question: what is our canonical supported matrix for Private (host kernel + driver combos)? Product, we need to make that explicit. Right now docs are ambiguous about "recommended" vs "supported".

aj: For immediate mitigation, advise the customer to roll back to the last known-good driver (525.x), or reboot into the older kernel if available. If they can't, we can try forcing module rebuild: 
```
sudo dkms autoinstall
modprobe -r nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia
modprobe nvidia
```
But if kernel-driver ABI mismatch exists, rollback is safer.

kevin: Also check for secure boot signatures blocking module load. If secure boot is enabled, unsigned modules will be rejected and you'll see similar failures.

tara-support: I'll give the rollback + dkms steps to the customer now. Also flagging that customer is asking for a formal matrix update.

maria: From infra side: maintaining certified combos across every enterprise kernel (RHEL kernels, Ubuntu HWE, custom vendor kernels) is expensive. We should align on what we legally guarantee vs recommended guidance for Private.

leo-sre: Proposed short-term plan: A) Help the customer rollback and validate B) Request access to failing node for deeper trace C) Create an internal doc listing the minimal validated host driver/kernel combos we test in CI.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-3825 - customer private cluster NCCL/driver failures. P1 assigned to eng-infra.

aj: Long-term discussion for Product: do we offer a paid "compatibility assurance" add-on for Private customers where we maintain and test specific kernel+driver permutations? That would cover support cost.

tara-support: Noted. Customer indicated willingness to pay for on-site validation if we had that offering.

maria: For now, can infra own a small matrix doc (readme) in our internal repo that we can link to support? I can draft.

kevin: If the customer gives node access, I'll try to capture: modinfo nvidia, dmesg, ldd of libnccl.so inside the runtime container, and check for multiple CUDA libs on PATH.

maria: Action items: 
- tara-support: share rollback + dkms steps and ask for node access (ETA 30m)
- kevin: be on standby for module/dmesg analysis if access granted
- leo-sre: spin up a reproducible lab node (6.1+535) or confirm we have one (ETA 2h)
- aj: draft an internal short doc: "Private host compatibility: recommended vs supported" (ETA EOD)

tara-support: Acked, pinging customer now.

maria: If we can't repro in 2h we'll escalate to oncall SRE and consider scheduling a controlled rollback window for the customer's private nodes.

oncall-bot: oncall@infra notified.

leo-sre: I'll check lab inventory and report back in the thread.

maria: Thanks all. Keeping thread open for logs and access details. :handshake:
